another reason to be always sitting on the rec pad lol
on the other hand when you are near the enemy base keep an eye out for the yellow dot on radar which means they have pods up
you can get a quick refill if no one is looking lol
one good strategy is to hover above base until people start to counter, and then when nobody is on the ground anymore you drop down to steal their pods and run away
or as scion you can morph while dropping to hit the con or upg before the enemies can react
most people dont play proactively, if they are hovering up to counter while you're already in base it's too late
that's how players like sly will run circles around you
basicly, be hovering before they arrive
Height matters in a hover fight

so for example if you see the enemies getting weps (not out on the field for a long time around the 5-7 min mark), and you think they will attack as their first move, you should hover up IMMEDIATELY before they arrive
its harder to aim up then it is to aim down
you can aim either direction but having height allows you to have more options for escape and movement
proactive counter hovering forces the attacker to face you before hitting your base
even if you die it still buys time
being below the opponent in a hover duel is often advantageous since you can use gravity to fall faster than they can approach you to get more range on your projectile weps
you'll notice when fighting really good players that it's hard to approach them if you have the higher altitude
assuming equal loadouts like two chain empties
normally my strategy if you are higher is to wait for the enemy to drop and then I drop with them, until they hit the ground and then I have the advantage
cyber hovering can prevent that cause the person below can slowly creep upwards
which is why it's so effective when defending
msl scout is a bit harder than xares I think
you need a good place to ramp off of to get speed quick, hovering up from flat ground will take a long time to gain height and speed
gotta really utilize strafe + S in the diagonal for max acceleration
since you have so much range you don't have to hover super perfectly though
got a big buffer against most units besides blast tanks which you got +30m on and another full scout or msl scout with 200m shad
I can post a video with a keyboard overlay
it's all about building up speed using the diagonal and conserving it by not turning too quick
when you see people spinning around or flipping that's to maintain the right angle

I added the bounding box of the nav to the position height placement. It was basically spawning *slightly* below the prop, especially on sloped surfaces.

NavBeacons always force themselves onto the ground when spawned. So, it was taking the position and snapping it to the ground (so if the Nav's spawn position was already slightly under the prop, it'd get set to the ground underneath, since that one's check starts at the height of the prop and looks down to find terrain height)
I looked into it, the nav placement code is 2D. It only knows the X/Z of where you order the NAV command to.
so, there's no relative height to "start" from. It just gets the terrain height. (which will always be the ground above tunnels)
Were navs *ever* able to be placed inside the little room in the Service Bay? or inside the Factory/Rec rooms, in any previous versions of BZ2?

See the 2D white line, there is clearly math to translate that to a 3D location.
HUD code sends the command to UserProcess, which AI commands use a 2D Vector
so the userprocess that spawns the nav has no Y component
There is also a short white line being drawn perpendicular from the surface. If nav placement was rewritten it could be used for orientation, like plant class placement from the editor.

I've never really seen you play but the #1 thing in bz2 is having high uptime, for both cmd and thug

Yeah ok sweet, and I suppose how you build or base will depend on the match?
to start I would focus less on fighting until you get used to multi tasking
the standard build order is to go upg, power, fac, arm, bay, 2nd power, tech, relay, blast tank
in between structures you are building scavs, empties, weapon crates etc. so in between those items are when you can dedicate more focus to fighting
the upgrade is very important since scavs, empties, and crates all take 20 scrap which is what an upgrade produces
an empty + crate is 20 seconds with an upgrade, 40 seconds without one
so likewise your strategy should revolve around guarding your own upgrade and destroying the enemy upgrade
That's why people make empties then make a crate, because the income is faster when staying below 20 rather than waiting for 30 to build custom empty
modding empties is a lot slower than dropping crates
Isn't red like 3 scrap per 1 second and orange is 1 scrap per second?
red is 2 per second, yellow 1, green 1 per 3 seconds
sometimes it's good to wait for green like 60->65 for a tank, but most of the time it's not
the first 2 minutes of a game are key as cmdr, which is what you should focus on the most
So how come people upgrade second pool in mid-late game?
second pool lets you mass produces rats, msl scouts, trucks, and any other 40-50 scrap unit
an upgrade lets you produce an item 10 scrap more expensive than red via empty cancelling

there's not really any expensive items that would make it worth getting

Sorry for the long post. (I know we just met, I played mostly MPI with some VSR back in the day - ((1998-2012ish))

I personally like elo ratings.

However, it appears to have rank weighting exclusively for W/L. Shouldn't there be rank weighting on points per game for elo as well? Under W/L rating, someone could theoretically always be paired with great players and have an artificially high elo despite not being a useful player. K/D and K/D+A with pvp points weighted higher than pve would help keep scoring more real.

Elo typically gives high bonuses for wins, lowers score for loss, but still favors in game performance k/d & kda with point weighting.

E.g. A player should theoretically be able to increase score slightly on a loss if in game performance was excellent. While significantly more difficult to increase elo on a loss, it should still be possible. Most of the time a good player would be capable of keeping elo unchanged or slightly better on a loss if the loss was not due to low performance.

Commanders would have to be rated differently. (Building and commanding performance. Crafts built vs crafts lost, highest tech achieved, scrap spent, etc.)

IMO, elo could be a great indicator of a player or commander's true capability if performance is weighted vs simply categorizing based on W/L.

It was a mix of issues. In addition I have a custom type-serializer I throw on to deal with the issues with string vs number consistency, where newtonsoft by default will just silently type coerce but Text.JSON won't and will exception instead.
using source generators as well now?

dont need to inject no context and it is more performant

my V2 API generates data as a stream of Datums that are fired out as they become available, either via a chunked connection as lines of JSON (ND-JSON) or as an event-source stream.

that said the VSR game list uses the V1 API I hope to kill off eventually.  Once V2 is stable I can work to either make a V1 wrapper that converts parts of V2 into V1 so I can kill normal V1, or we can try to update the vsr game list code

The reason I like this "datums as they become available" method is that it is a big step to live data flow rather than polling, and it will also allow for very slow components, like checking if a player in a session is currently live-streaming said session to twitch.  That datum can come down whole seconds later and decorate a webpage that's otherwise already finished.

I've noticed a lot of bad communication in games lately, so here are some `rat flare tips`:

use informational callouts sparingly: for example
> they're hitting our 2nd
is not a good callout because you don't know WHO is hitting it, is it an empty or a blast tank? how many people? your team won't be able to respond effectively without context. Is the 2nd even a priority? If you have 5 pools already or are using red scrap to arm your team it doesn't even matter in the short term. Instead make it actionable by saying something like
> empty hitting our second, defend it (implies whole team, or task a specific player nearby)

Callouts like
> inc on base
or
> arm up
are good because it updates your team on the state of the game and they can infer what to do from there. If it's not something you would want to type out in text chat it's probably not important enough to say in voice. Especially avoid making callouts on information that's only relevant to you or has no effect on the game, like
> grok and gemini are chain
chain is a normal thing to get and you'd expect that anyways
> grok and gemini are PUMMEL?!
pummel is NOT normal and it probably means you're going to get rec rushed, that's an important callout and you should probably add if they are incoming and from where
This is important because flooding comms will distract people from more important information at best, and make people mute or leave comms at worst

@Lithium the snipe stats are currently buggedd
sometimes i question the amount of pods getting counted but maybe it really is that high
at some point ill go and verify every single datapoint to make sure its legit

its a bit of a convulated calculation: at it's core its: `50%"did you leave base?", 30% "did you push far compared to the match's biggest pushers?", 20% "did you keep moving compared to the match's busiest movers?"` average it, multiply by 100

Say in a match:

1. you spent 30% of your samples inside base -> time_in_base_pct = 0.30
2. your furthest push was 4,800m-> max_dist = 4800
3. the match's 95th-percentile push was 5,200 -> p95_max_dist_in_match = 5200
4. uou averaged 60 m/s of ground covered -> path_length_per_sec = 60
5 thhe match's 95th-percentile of that was 75 -> p95_path_per_sec_in_match = 75

in math terms:

time term =  0.5* (1 − 0.30) = 0.5 * 0.70= 0.350
dist term =  0.3 * min(4800/5200, 1.0)= 0.3 * 0.923= 0.277
path term =  0.2 * min(60/75, 1.0) = 0.2 * 0.800=0.160
sum  = 0.787

activity_score = round(100*0.787) = 79  ->  Mobile band (61–80)

so.....not aggressive but if you wanted that particular scenario to reach aggresive (≥81) youd need to either spend less time in base, or finish closer he top of the roster on max_dist or path_per_sec
its taking into account more than one factor `movemint`
not only leaving base, but also how much you move in general, how much you move compared to other players
my docs are admittedely way too complicated. will work to simplify them greatly at some point

if you decide to dig into the data yourself, here's some starter info:

- I have ~90 good matches worth of raw vtstat data here: https://github.com/sevsunday/vt-stats/tree/main/data/sessions
- you can decode with protobuf in a language of your choice, i always use python these days
- the vtstats binpb is based on the proto schema here: https://github.com/VTrider/statsgate/blob/main/statsgate.proto
- binpbs contain every single tick of the match, and tracks these events: BulletInit, BulletHit, DamageDealt, UpdateTick (for position, t-key, ODF), UnitDestroyed, UnitSniped, and PickupPowerup + the StatHeader for steamids and other match metadata
- currently the binpbs are missing sonic wave data entirely, as well as win/loss outcomes
- if you want to include win / loss outcomes based on f9's games you'd have to join them by hand - just match them up based on f9's timestamps and the timestamps in the statheader/metadata 
- if you have trouble decoding the raw binpb files, you can download the decoded JSONS of each match here (unfortunately only one at a time, i generate it on the fly): https://vtstats.bz/raw.html

data cleanup:
- make sure you properly identify campod players (odf property in UpdateTick) to ignore them
- if you see any damage events with a value of 1e6, ignore them. these are engine anomalies

why are we reinventing the wheel what was the issue be4
we were trying to solve the problem of not being able to drop command in a 10 player lobby

the old give/take command system worked like this:

When you Give Command, it MOVES you from Team 1 or 6, to the first EMPTY slot on your Team (max 5)
the probably i think we all voted with a misunderstanding of how the user experience would change
so if your team was full, clicking Give Command did nothing
this is a design flaw in the original system
which is why giving command on a full team did not work

The only way to solve it was to make the Give Command button trigger a "Pending" state, which enabled the Take Command button for thugs. But wait until one of the Thugs takes command, then SWAP the player's teams on the same turn
as a bonus he got rid of the resync too
so far, i still prefer the old way - but ill give this one some time to see what others feel/think as well

So. The reason why I say, reduce it's health over reducing it's mobility is that the Sentry's hyper mobility is part of the unit's identity, which is important. It's what makes it fun to pilot. It's survivability should come from it's movement, not it's ability to soak shots. If we reduce the damage or the range of the Gauss Gun, we then reduce the damage of every Scion unit that uses the the Gauss Gun. Likewise, we could reduce the effect of the Statis Shield, but then we're screwing over every other shield capable ship in the Scion Arsenal. Putting Scion's into the situation of "Absorption or die"
